title: [YouPass Collect] - Social Media Usage by Gender in Australia in 2011 & 2014
prompt: The following pie charts show the use of social media by men and women in Australia in 2011 and 2014. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts compare the frequency of social media usage among men and women in Australia in two separate years, 2011 and 2014.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, both genders showed an increasing trend toward daily social media use over the period. By 2014, daily usage had become the most common pattern for both men and women, with women demonstrating consistently higher engagement rates than their male counterparts.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding frequent usage patterns, in 2011, 30% of women used social media every day, slightly higher than men at 25%. By 2014, these figures had surged dramatically, with women's daily usage nearly doubling to 59%, while men's proportion increased to 45%. Meanwhile, the percentage of users accessing social media a few times a week declined for both genders, falling from 22% to 9% among women and from 19% to 16% among men.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for less frequent usage, once-a-week users accounted for 40% of women and 12% of men in 2011. However, by 2014, both groups experienced substantial decreases, with women's figures dropping to 10% and men's to 9%. Regarding non-users, the proportions showed divergent trends: while 44% of men never used social media in 2011, this figure declined to 30% by 2014. Conversely, women who never engaged with such platforms increased from 8% to 22% over the same period.
